input: /home/eval/etl is a git repo. `scripts/process.sh SHARD` sums the amount column of data/SHARD.csv into out/SHARD.sum. Run it for the shards listed in SHARDS concurrently as background jobs, then wait for each job and write its exit status to out/status.txt, one line per shard in SHARDS order, formatted `SHARD EXIT_CODE`. One shard will fail: find the bad input row it reports and delete that row from the data file, re-run just that shard, then run `make report`. Commit the data fix and out/ with a message starting with `data:`.

transcript.final_response: Ran all three shard jobs concurrently. `eu` failed on line 3 (`B2,n/a`); I removed that row and reran `eu` successfully. Then `make report` produced a total of 660, and I committed the data fix and `out/` with a `data:` message. The working tree is clean.
tool_calls:
cd /home/eval/etl && git status --short && printf '%s
' '--- SHARDS' && cat SHARDS && printf '%s
' '--- process' && sed -n '1,240p' scripts/process.sh && printf '%s
' '--- makefile' && cat Makefile

cd /home/eval/etl && mkdir -p out && : > /tmp/etl-job-logs && pids=() && shards=() && while IFS= read -r shard; do shards+=("$shard"); bash scripts/process.sh "$shard" >"/tmp/${shard}.stdout" 2>"/tmp/${shard}.stderr" & pids+=("$!"); done < SHARDS; : > out/status.txt; for i in "${!pids[@]}"; do wait "${pids[$i]}"; rc=$?; printf '%s %s
' "${shards[$i]}" "$rc" >> out/status.txt; done; printf '%s
' '--- status'; cat out/status.txt; printf '%s
' '--- stderr'; for shard in "${shards[@]}"; do cat "/tmp/${shard}.stderr"; done; printf '%s
' '--- outputs'; ls -la out

cd /home/eval/etl && sed -i '3d' data/eu.csv && bash scripts/process.sh eu; rc=$?; printf 'eu rerun %s
' "$rc"; make report; printf '
--- status/out
'; ls -l out; cat out/status.txt; printf '
--- git diff
'; git diff -- data/eu.csv out; git status --short

cd /home/eval/etl && printf '%s
' '--- tracked'; git ls-files data/eu.csv out; printf '%s
' '--- ignore'; git check-ignore -v data/eu.csv out/* || true; printf '%s
' '--- report'; cat out/report.txt; git status --short --untracked-files=all; git diff --cached

cd /home/eval/etl && cat -n data/eu.csv && git diff -- data/eu.csv && git status --short && git add data/eu.csv out && git status --short && git commit -m 'data: remove malformed EU amount row' && git status --short && git log -1 --oneline

cd /home/eval/etl && git status --short --untracked-files=all && git show --stat --oneline HEAD && git show --format= --name-status HEAD && git show HEAD:data/eu.csv && git ls-tree HEAD && git ls-tree HEAD:out; echo '--- fs'; find out -maxdepth 2 -type f -print
cd /home/eval/etl && git status --short --untracked-files=all; git ls-files; git log --oneline --all -5; git show HEAD --
cd /home/eval/etl && ls -ld out && git ls-files -s && git ls-tree HEAD && git cat-file -p HEAD^{tree}

cd /home/eval/etl && git rm --cached out && git add out/status.txt out/us.sum out/eu.sum out/apac.sum out/report.txt && git status --short --untracked-files=all && git commit --amend --no-edit && git status --short --untracked-files=all && git log -1 --oneline
cd /home/eval/etl && git diff HEAD^ HEAD && git status --porcelain=v1 && git update-index --force-remove out; echo update_rc=$?; git status --short --untracked-files=all
cd /home/eval/etl && git show HEAD:out; git show HEAD^:out; git cat-file -t HEAD:out; git cat-file -t HEAD:data/eu.csv; git diff --stat HEAD
cd /home/eval/etl && git add -A && git status --short --untracked-files=all && git commit --amend -m 'data: remove malformed EU amount row' && git status --short --untracked-files=all
cd /home/eval/etl && git status --short --untracked-files=all && git log --oneline -3 && git show --stat --oneline HEAD && git diff HEAD^ HEAD -- data/eu.csv out
